title: Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager: assess Microsoft Foundry agents against AI regulations
notes: claim 54: severity major on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Hold: the assessment-creation wizard is presented as a control over who can create assessments, but it does not assign permissions. The Foundry role command also assigns access at project scope, whereas the integration prerequisites require a role on the relevant Foundry accounts.

claims.claim: Assigning Foundry User with az role assignment create --role 53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d --assignee <user> --scope <project-id> supplies the role needed to add agents to Compliance Manager.
claims.quote: The admin account must have either the Azure AI Project Manager or Azure AI User RBAC role assigned to the relevant AI Foundry accounts.
claims.fix: Replace the call with 'az role assignment create --role 53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d --assignee <user> --scope <foundry-resource-id>'. Set api.docs to https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/concepts/rbac-foundry, which documents this command and resource-level assignments. Define the scope placeholder in the note as the relevant Foundry account/resource's Azure resource ID, not a project's ID. The CLI reference at https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/role/assignment confirms all parameters; Azure RBAC scope documentation states lower levels inherit from higher levels, not that project assignments grant parent-account access.
